title: A zero nobody proved could be non-zero

candidates.pattern: Validate a measuring harness against a known-zero before believing a number it produces
candidates.failurePrevented: A harness reports a plausible zero because it measured nothing, and the zero gets believed precisely because it looks clean.
candidates.jclawEvidence: AGENTS.md:825 `**Validate a measurement harness against a known-zero case** before trusting a number it produces. Time a no-op; assert on an empty input. A harness that reports plausible nonsense is worse than no measurement, because it gets believed.` Operationalised in .claude/commands/secret-scan.md:40 `**Prove the harness before trusting a zero.** Before reporting anything, run a known-positive control — `git grep -cP 'looksLikeSecret' -- test` must be non-zero ... A pass that has not been shown capable of matching is not evidence of absence`.
candidates.builtAndExercised: Yes, and it was retrofitted after a real false-CLEAN: commit f588bc44 2026-08-15 `fix(secret-scan): the documented invocation could not match anything` measured `-E detected 0 of 9` vs `-P detected 9 of 9` over nine planted synthetic credentials.
candidates.ourEvidence: HAVE for the two big gates: tests/claimcheck.test.ts:334-335 `expect(cites).toBeGreaterThan(1600); expect(values).toBeGreaterThan(350);` and tests/chaosGate.test.ts:73 reads `const EXPECTED_TOTAL = (\d+);` out of scripts/gates/chaos.ts rather than restating it. GAP in one place: .githooks/pre-commit:40 `grep -E '^ *(Test Files|Tests) +[0-9]' "$log" | sed 's/^ */      /' || true` — the hook's own comment (lines 36-38) says two commit messages asserted the wrong test totals and 'A number on screen cannot be inferred from memory', yet if vitest's reporter format changes the grep matches nothing, prints nothing, and `|| true` keeps the commit green with no number on screen at all. Our memory feedback-probe-parser-must-match records exactly this happening once already (Node 26 spec reporter hid 3 chaos results).
candidates.proposal: In .githooks/pre-commit's run_step, capture the grep output and fail the step when the tests log yields no totals line, instead of `|| true`.
candidates.doneCriterion: Point the hook at a log whose totals line does not match the pattern → the hook exits non-zero saying the totals could not be read; restore → green printing `Tests 1631 passed (1631)`.
candidates.cost: ~4 lines in an existing function; 0 tokens per turn.
candidates.why: It is the one unguarded zero-reporter left in our gate chain, in the same file whose comment records the defect it fails to prevent.

candidates.pattern: A fail-open branch carries its reason on the line, and never hides a measurement
candidates.failurePrevented: A gate silently switches itself off — the run looks identical to a clean pass, which is the fail-open-accounting killer applied to a hook.
candidates.jclawEvidence: .githooks/pre-commit:103-108 `# Skip when lint-staged isn't installed (e.g. a fresh clone before # `pnpm install` runs in frontend/). Fail open rather than blocking commits.` — and it PRINTS on the way out: `[jclaw pre-commit] lint-staged not installed yet — skipping.` Same shape at :136-139 for pnpm. The contrast is app/services/scanners/Scanner.java, whose javadoc makes fail-open a written contract ('Implementations MUST fail open: network errors, timeouts, quota exhaustion ... MUST return Verdict.clean()') against test/ShellExecSandboxTest.java's 'an unavailable mechanism fails closed'.
candidates.builtAndExercised: Yes — 9cd7059a 2026-09-08 `fix(hooks): find pnpm before exec'ing lint-staged; fail open when absent`. The Scanner contrast is critic.json #11, whose paths and quotes I re-read.
candidates.ourEvidence: Our two fail-opens differ in quality. REASONED AND HARMLESS: .githooks/pre-commit:11-12 `# Skip inside CI (CI runs its own checks).` + `[ -n "$CI" ] && exit 0`. CORRECTION to an earlier draft, which asserted SSHD has no CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml exists and its header reads `# Push-time verification — mirrors the local .githooks/pre-commit gate, plus the full vite build`, running `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run build` on push to master and on pull_request. The skip is therefore correct rather than dead — and moot besides, since GitHub Actions does not execute git hooks. SILENT AND WRONG: .githooks/pre-commit:40 `grep -E '^ *(Test Files|Tests) +[0-9]' "$log" | sed 's/^ */      /' || true` — if the reporter format moves, no totals print and the commit proceeds, while lines 36-38 of that same file record two commit messages (3adac1b, 8f332e9) that asserted 1002/1003 tests when the hook had measured 1001.
candidates.proposal: Same fix as agent-instructions-4: make the totals grep fail the step when it matches nothing. Leave the CI skip alone but print one line when it fires.
candidates.why: Merges with agent-instructions-4 — same file, same line, same defect class arriving from two directions, which is itself the argument that it is the right fix.

candidates.pattern: A detector must be shown capable of matching before a zero from it is reported
candidates.failurePrevented: A scan written in a regex dialect its engine does not implement matches nothing, and the resulting CLEAN is believed precisely because it looks like health.
candidates.jclawEvidence: Commit f588bc44 2026-08-15 `fix(secret-scan): the documented invocation could not match anything`: `On macOS git (Apple Git 2.50.1) the ERE engine silently ignores \b, \d and \s — no error, no warning, just zero matches. Fifteen of the sixteen CRITICAL patterns are \b-anchored ... The lone exception was the PEM pattern ... which is exactly why the failure looked like a clean repo rather than a broken tool.` Measured in the body: `-E detected 0 of 9 / -P detected 9 of 9`. The durable fix is the control, .claude/commands/secret-scan.md:40 `**Prove the harness before trusting a zero.** ... A pass that has not been shown capable of matching is not evidence of absence`.
candidates.builtAndExercised: Yes — the control is a mandatory documented step whose result the report template must state, added in the same commit as the fix. Honest limit: it is enforced by instruction, not by a test.
candidates.ourEvidence: The dialect hazard REPRODUCES on this machine but has no live site: in a scratch repo containing `abcd` and `abc 123`, `git grep -nE '\d'` returned `f.txt:1:abcd` (literal d) while `git grep -nP '\d'` returned `f.txt:2:abc 123`; and `grep -rn 'git grep -E'` over our *.sh, *.ts, *.mjs and *.md → empty. The control DISCIPLINE we mostly have: tests/claimcheck.test.ts:334-335 floors the corpus at >1600 cites / >350 values, tests/chaosGate.test.ts:73 reads the runner's own constant. One unguarded zero-reporter remains — .githooks/pre-commit:40's `|| true` totals grep (agent-instructions-4).
candidates.proposal: None beyond agent-instructions-4. Record the `git grep -E` hazard as a pitfall line rather than a gate, since we have nothing to guard.
candidates.why: The discipline is already ours and already applied; the specific macOS trap has zero live sites here. Adopting the fix we do need (the `|| true`) and dropping the rest loudly is the honest split.

candidates.pattern: A live-match FLOOR beside every scan that could match nothing, plus a sanity probe that the scan is reading the right corpus — so a predicate that silently stops matching cannot pass vacuously (and a frozen store cannot be pruned to empty on a regeneration run).
candidates.failurePrevented: A gate that reads '0 failures' because its matcher stopped matching — the exact shape of claimcheck's first version ('0 failures' over four wrong cites).
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/CapabilityRulesTest.java:46-49 "Each frozen rule is paired with a floor on the live match count. It guards the deliberate regeneration run, when the store switches are on: a predicate that had silently stopped matching ... would then prune the store to empty and pass forever." :348-354 assertFloor(). test/WallClockDisciplineTest.java:117-119 "no call to utils.AppClock found in the imported classes — the scan is looking at the wrong bytecode and every rule below would pass vacuously". test/ArchitectureTest.java:154-156 "the scan matched nothing and would pass vacuously".
candidates.builtAndExercised: BUILT: FROZEN_PROCESS_SPAWNER_FILES=17 (CapabilityRulesTest.java:62), FROZEN_DIRECT_PATH_FILES=5 (:98), FROZEN_INTERVAL_FILES=18 (WallClockDisciplineTest.java:49), KNOWN_ALLOWLIST_GATED_CONTROLLERS=2 (ArchitectureTest.java:112). Commit 245ddc1f added the wall-clock floor when it moved the store to a named file.
candidates.ourEvidence: SSHD tests/claimcheck.test.ts:329-335 "A guard against the gate quietly shrinking — a resolver bug that drops most cites would otherwise read as a clean pass" `expect(cites).toBeGreaterThan(1600); expect(values).toBeGreaterThan(350);`. tests/config-purity.test.ts:52 `expect(files.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` plus a 16-row caught/4-row clean scanner self-test (:78-101). tests/chaosGate.test.ts:41 EXPECTED_PLANTS = 43 and :69-73 reads chaos.ts's EXPECTED_TOTAL so the two copies cannot drift. tests/configTwins.test.ts `expect(TWINS).toHaveLength(36)`. Fail-closed discovery: chaosGate.test.ts:53-61 on-disk *.plants.ts must equal the statically imported set. The one scan with no explicit floor is game-purity-ratchet (13 files), but its scanner is the one config-purity self-tests, and 'every game/ file is baselined' fails on a new file.
candidates.proposal: None beyond -1 (its stale-file check is the missing baseline ⊆ current half). Nothing else to add.
candidates.doneCriterion: n/a — already observable: tests/claimcheck.test.ts and tests/chaosGate.test.ts are green with their floors in place.
candidates.why: We already have it, on every gate JClaw would have it on, and ours came from the same lesson (claimcheck false-passing). Recorded so nobody claims this as a gap.

candidates.pattern: Validate the harness against a known-zero AND a known-one before trusting it, and pin that a scan 'scanned at all' — an absence-assertion over an empty set passes vacuously.
candidates.failurePrevented: "a harness that reports plausible nonsense is worse than no harness, because it gets believed" — a challenge page scored as content at 60%; an ArchUnit-style rule over zero matched classes; an empty pass-rate denominator reading as 100%.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/ScrapeHarnessTest.java:21-23 "The known-zero and known-one cases are the point: a harness that reports plausible nonsense is worse than no harness, because it gets believed" + knownZero_aChallengePageIsNeverScoredAsContent (:52), knownOne_aRealArticleScoresOk (:58); evals/scrape/README.md:97-98 "a URL that always challenges must score 0%, not 60%"; test/ErrorCodeCentralisationTest.java:122 scannedTheTreeAtAllRatherThanPassingVacuously `assertTrue(javaFiles > 300 …)`; test/ArchitectureTest.java:154-156 "the scan matched nothing and would pass vacuously"; test/McpConnectionManagerTest.java:215-217 "Known-zero guard: without a single non-CONNECTED sample the loop above asserted nothing"; app/services/evals/EvalReport.java:76-77 "An empty suite — or one where every case errored — scores 0 rather than a vacuous 1."
candidates.builtAndExercised: All of the above are committed JUnit tests in test/; EvalSuiteConformanceTest.java:68-81 additionally requires every check kind to be used by a shipped suite.
candidates.ourEvidence: HAVE almost everywhere: tests/claimcheck.test.ts:320-330 "A guard against the gate quietly shrinking … expect(cites).toBeGreaterThan(1600); expect(values).toBeGreaterThan(350)"; tests/chaosGate.test.ts:191 'refuses a run that collected NO tests, even though it exited 0'; agent-harness chaos.e2e.test.mjs:61 'a covered guard goes RED and an uncovered one is a MISSING TEST' (known-one + known-zero in one e2e); measure-refute.test.mjs:46 every-alive → VERIFIED/fatalCount 0 and :53 every-dead → UNVERIFIED/null; scripts/gauntlet/wfcheck.mjs:12-17 runs both branches; tests/chaosGate.test.ts:59 'imports exactly the *.plants.ts files that are on disk'. The one weak floor: tests/config-purity.test.ts:53 `expect(files.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);` guards the ZERO-numeric-literal absence-assertion over src/core with a floor of 1, while `git ls-files src/core | grep -c '\.ts$'` → 64 today — a lister that dropped 60 of 64 files would still pass.
candidates.proposal: tests/config-purity.test.ts:53: replace `toBeGreaterThan(0)` with a measured floor `toBeGreaterThan(40)` and a one-line comment naming the 64 measured on 2026-09-14 (same idiom as claimcheck.test.ts:322-324).
candidates.doneCriterion: `npx vitest run tests/config-purity.test.ts` green; chaos-probe by temporarily changing `listTsFiles` to return `files.slice(0, 3)` → the test goes red naming the count; restore byte-identical.
candidates.why: The pattern is already our house rule (global CLAUDE.md 'a gate that says 0 is probed for false-passes first') and held by every gate but this one; config-purity is the invariant `src/core has ZERO numeric literals` that the repo's CLAUDE.md lists first, and its vacuity floor is 1 file.

candidates.pattern: The harness repo's own test command must fail on zero tests and pin a floor — `node --test <glob>` passes when the glob matches nothing
candidates.failurePrevented: agent-harness is PUBLIC and its only documented verification is `node --test 'harness/**/*.test.mjs'`. Move a test file, misquote the glob, or run from the wrong directory and Node reports `# tests 0`, `# fail 0`, exit 0 — 'all tests pass'. There is no package.json, no hook, no count pin in that repo, and its two docs already disagree on the count.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/TestDiscoveryConformanceTest.java:63-64 "A scan that silently matched nothing would report the same empty list as a clean tree." / `assertTrue(examined > 400, ...)`; test/SidecarDefaultPortsConformanceTest.java:28-29 "a regex that silently stopped matching must not pass by finding none" + `KNOWN_MANAGERS = 7`; AGENTS.md:32 "Never pipe the suite (`| tail` returns tail's exit code); redirect to a file".
candidates.builtAndExercised: JClaw: the floor idiom appears in 4 of the 8 files read (TestDiscovery >400, ResourceLeak >=7 and >=20, SpaBuildInputs KNOWN_ESCAPING_IMPORTS=14, SidecarDefaultPorts KNOWN_MANAGERS=7), all committed and running in `play autotest`. OUR side MEASURED: `node --test 'zz-nope/**/*.test.mjs'` on Node v26.8.1 → exit 0, tap summary `# tests 0 / # pass 0 / # fail 0`; an explicit missing FILE (`node --test /tmp/zz-nope.test.mjs`) → exit 1. So the glob form is the fail-open one.
candidates.ourEvidence: agent-harness/harness/README.md:130 "**Check it yourself:** `node --test 'harness/**/*.test.mjs'` — 43 tests."; agent-harness/RESUME_HERE.md:9 "VERIFY: `node --test harness/` → 24 pass" (two numbers for one suite); `ls agent-harness` → no package.json; `ls agent-harness/.githooks` → does not exist; `grep -hoE '^\s*test\(' harness/*/*.test.mjs | wc -l` → 41 (loops/each not counted — not reconciled with 43). SSHD is fine on this axis: vitest's `passWithNoTests` defaults false and chaosLib.baselineIsGreen requires `passed > 0` (scripts/gates/chaosLib.ts:75-78).
candidates.proposal: agent-harness/harness/test.sh (≈8 lines, committed, referenced from README and RESUME_HERE in place of the bare command): `node --test --test-reporter=tap 'harness/**/*.test.mjs' > "$log" 2>&1; code=$?`; then `grep -q '^# fail 0$' "$log"` and `n=$(sed -n 's/^# tests //p' "$log")`, `[ "$n" -ge 40 ]` else print the summary block and exit 1. Node's own `--test-reporter=tap` is used because the spec reporter on Node 26 prints `ℹ tests` (memory: 'Node 26 spec reporter hid 3 chaos results'). Also fix RESUME_HERE.md:9 to the measured count.
candidates.doneCriterion: `sh harness/test.sh` → prints `# tests 4x` and exits 0; `sh harness/test.sh` after `mv harness/chaos/chaosLib.test.mjs /tmp/` → exits 1 on the floor (restore). Running it from a wrong cwd → exits 1, never 0.
candidates.cost: ~8 lines of sh + 2 doc lines; 0 dependencies (the repo's whole point); ~15 min.
candidates.why: The harness that teaches 'a probe whose parser matched nothing has not passed' (harness/README.md rule 6) currently verifies itself with exactly such a probe. Floor + fail-closed, not an exact pin, so adding tests does not churn it (JClaw's choice too).

candidates.pattern: A skip-guarded suite must fail, not skip, when the thing it is guarded on is present but the guard's own probe drifted — 'a checker switched off' must go red
candidates.failurePrevented: Ten byte-check suites are each guarded by their own `existsSync(<one specific file>)`. Rename or move one reference file (or the whole tree) and that suite skips; vitest prints `N skipped` on the Tests line, the pre-commit prints that line and still commits. The suite reads green with a transcription gate switched off. JClaw's AGENTS.md names the mirror image for its frontend ("in a fresh worktree run nuxi prepare first or the suite false-REDs with zero tests"); ours false-GREENs, the worse direction.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/NullnessGateConformanceTest.java:17-19 "nothing in the suite would notice the gate being switched off, downgraded to a warning, or left behind by a new subpackage"; :35-37 SILENT_SWITCH_OFFS list; test/ResourceLeakGateConformanceTest.java:94-95 "A hierarchy walk that silently stopped resolving would pass this test on an empty set." + `assertTrue(scanned.size() >= 7, ...)`.
candidates.builtAndExercised: JClaw: commit 88b142ee 2026-09-06 "test(gates): close the silent switch-offs the conformance tests could not see (JCLAW-1149, JCLAW-1156, ...)" — the second iteration, i.e. the first version of these guards was itself found fail-open and closed.
candidates.ourEvidence: `grep -rnE 'const (HAVE_SOURCE|HAVE_BINDATA|hasReference) =' tests` → 10 definitions in 10 files, each on a DIFFERENT file (ogAiData.test.ts:154 `existsSync(path.join(SCRIPTS, 'NPCManager.as'))`, npcTree.test.ts:33 `'NPC.as'`, ogItemData.test.ts:221 `ITEMDATA`, composePose.test.ts:228 `BINDATA`, ...). Only claimcheck.test.ts:309-316 makes the skip loud (`process.stdout.write('[claimcheck] SKIPPED: ... This is not a pass.')`) and it only writes; nothing FAILS. .githooks/pre-commit:39-41 greps the `Tests` line and prints it — no assertion on `skipped`. RESUME_HERE.md:19 records the healthy shape `Tests 1631 passed (1631)` (no skipped segment). `reference/decompiled/shs3_android_payload/scripts` exists on this machine (ls → yes), so today 0 skip.
candidates.proposal: .githooks/pre-commit, inside `run_step` after the tests grep (4 lines): `if [ "$1" = tests ] && [ -d reference/decompiled/shs3_android_payload/scripts ] && grep -qE '^ *Tests .*skipped' "$log"; then printf '❌ tests SKIPPED with reference/ present — a byte-check guard drifted. Not a pass.\n'; exit 1; fi`. (With gate-guards-1 in place `.only` is caught earlier; this catches the ten skipIf guards, which `.only` does not cover.) Do NOT consolidate the ten `existsSync`s into one constant — each guards a different file on purpose; the hook-level assertion is the one place that sees them all.
candidates.doneCriterion: Chaos-style check by hand: edit tests/ogItemData.test.ts:221 to point ITEMDATA at a bogus path, stage a trivial .ts change, `git commit` → refused with 'tests SKIPPED with reference/ present'; revert → commit proceeds and the printed line has no `skipped`.
candidates.cost: 4 lines of sh; 0 per-turn tokens; ~10 min including the by-hand red/green.
candidates.why: JClaw asserts the checker's wiring from inside a test; for us the cheapest single point that sees every skip is the hook's already-parsed summary line. A test cannot read its own run's skip count.
